pages.text: Madam Salamatu gave each pair of pupils a magnet and a cloth bag of everyday items. “Let us find out what the magnet can pick up,” she said. Zaara and Worla opened their notebook ready to record what happened.
sentences: Madam Salamatu gave each pair of pupils a magnet and a cloth bag of everyday items.
“Let us find out what the magnet can pick up,” she said.
Zaara and Worla opened their notebook ready to record what happened.
pages.alt: At a wooden classroom desk, Zaara holds a red-and-blue magnet while Worla opens a plain notebook beside a cloth bag of small classroom objects as Madam Salamatu smiles nearby.

pages.text: First, they tested an iron nail. Click! It jumped straight onto the magnet. A paper clip jumped up too, and so did a steel pin. “They all have iron in them,” explained Madam Salamatu. “Steel is made mainly from iron.”
sentences: First, they tested an iron nail.
Click!
It jumped straight onto the magnet.
A paper clip jumped up too, and so did a steel pin.
“They all have iron in them,” explained Madam Salamatu.
“Steel is made mainly from iron.”
pages.alt: Close view on the wooden desk as Zaara’s red-and-blue magnet lifts an iron nail, a silver paper clip, and a small steel pin together.

pages.text: Next, they tested a pencil, a green leaf, a plastic spoon, a wooden stick, and a smooth glass marble. None of them moved at all. “A magnet pulls only certain metals,” said Madam Salamatu. “Even shiny aluminium foil does not stick to it.”
sentences: Next, they tested a pencil, a green leaf, a plastic spoon, a wooden stick, and a smooth glass marble.
None of them moved at all.
“A magnet pulls only certain metals,” said Madam Salamatu.
“Even shiny aluminium foil does not stick to it.”
pages.alt: Zaara holds the magnet near a yellow pencil, green leaf, blue plastic spoon, small wooden stick, glass marble, and piece of foil resting motionless on the desk.

pages.text: Then Zaara placed a sheet of paper over the iron nail and held the magnet just above the paper. The nail slid right along with the magnet! “Magnets can pull through thin paper,” she said happily.
sentences: Then Zaara placed a sheet of paper over the iron nail and held the magnet just above the paper.
The nail slid right along with the magnet!
“Magnets can pull through thin paper,” she said happily.
pages.alt: Zaara moves the red-and-blue magnet above a plain white sheet of paper while Worla points happily at the iron nail sliding underneath.

pages.text: Next, they tested two bar magnets together. When opposite ends met, they pulled close with a snap. When Worla turned one magnet around, the matching ends pushed apart. “Opposite ends pull,” said Worla, “and same ends push.”
sentences: Next, they tested two bar magnets together.
When opposite ends met, they pulled close with a snap.
When Worla turned one magnet around, the matching ends pushed apart.
“Opposite ends pull,” said Worla, “and same ends push.”
pages.alt: Zaara and Worla holding two red-and-blue bar magnets face-to-face above their desk, feeling the invisible push between two matching red ends.

pages.text: Before collecting the magnets, Madam Salamatu shared an important safety rule. “Magnets are science tools, not toys for toddlers,” she said. “Never put a magnet near your mouth, because swallowing one is very dangerous. Always store magnets safely away from little children.”
sentences: Before collecting the magnets, Madam Salamatu shared an important safety rule.
“Magnets are science tools, not toys for toddlers,” she said.
“Never put a magnet near your mouth, because swallowing one is very dangerous.
Always store magnets safely away from little children.”
pages.alt: Madam Salamatu carefully placing the red-and-blue magnets into a sturdy lidded storage box on her high teacher’s desk while Zaara and Worla nod attentively.

activities.question: What do the nail, paper clip, and steel pin all have in them?
Which of these did the magnet NOT pick up?

activities.prompt: Put the magnet tests in order.
items: Test an iron nail and a paper clip.
Test a pencil, a leaf, and a plastic spoon.
Pull a nail through a sheet of paper.
Test how two magnets pull and push.

activities.definition: Completely different or facing the other way.

glossary.definition: An object that pulls things made of iron or steel.
A hard grey metal that magnets pull.
A strong metal made mainly from iron.
